title: SyncManifest
description: What one run of musubi did, or -- when kind is 'plan' -- what it would have done. musubi is the reference producer, not required to be the only one. THIS SCHEMA DESCRIBES SHAPE ONLY: it cannot check that run_id re-derives, that the coverage totals add up, or that a removal names a unit that was emitted. See docs/contracts.md, section 'What these schemas cannot say'.

contract.description: A consumer that does not recognise this value refuses the manifest rather than guessing at it (ADR-0002). The -draft suffix is a state of the contract register, not a property of this document: a draft and a frozen manifest of the same contract have the same shape, because freezing constrains what future versions may do. Whether the freeze has happened is in docs/contracts.md, which can be corrected; a schema saying so would go on saying it after the freeze.

run_id.description: sha256 over exactly the inputs that determined the output, canonicalized by RFC 8785 (ADR-0015). NOT created_at, so two runs of the same input share an id. NOT the source's root path, so the same corpus on two machines has the same id. NOT CHECKED HERE: that it re-derives -- that is what `musubi verify` is for, and no schema can do it.

kind.description: 'plan' wrote nothing (ADR-0012); 'sync' promoted what it staged. Both run the same pipeline and share a run_id, because the kind is metadata about which command was typed rather than about what the run would produce.

created_at.description: When the run happened. Metadata, and deliberately excluded from run_id.

rulesets.description: The cleansing packs in force. Every rule in them carries its own evidence and review date (ADR-0009); this names which packs, at which version.

converters.description: Which implementations built this corpus, so that a re-derivation can use the same ones.

screener.description: The instrument that looked for credentials. Its recall is a property of that instrument, and this names it so a reader can go and look it up (ADR-0017).

removals.description: Every firing of every cleansing rule. Long and boring on purpose: an account nobody reads is still an account somebody CAN read, and the alternative is an artefact that cannot be appealed (ADR-0005).

skipped.description: Everything seen and not carried, with its reason. A run that says '412 documents' and nothing else cannot be told apart from one that quietly excluded half the folder.

findings.description: Everything the screener matched, including hits that were allowed. A hit that was waved through is still a hit somebody should be able to find later.

allowed.description: rule:unit_key pairs the owner looked at and decided against. Recorded because an exemption nobody can see is an exemption that outlives its reason (ADR-0008).

withdrawn.description: Artefacts taken out of the corpus because the unit they came from is no longer in the source. A corpus keeping a document its owner deleted answers questions from something they withdrew, so removing it is correctness rather than tidiness -- and naming which ones is the same obligation as naming what was skipped. Only ever a path the previous manifest listed: musubi deletes what it recorded writing, and never what it merely found.

coverage.description: The denominators, published beside the numerators. `emitted` alone would let a reader compute a ratio against the wrong total, and they would.

limits.description: What this document does not say, carried IN the document rather than in the documentation, because the artefact travels and the documentation does not. A manifest with none is a manifest claiming it has none.

span.description: A half-open range, [start, end). NOT CHECKED HERE: that end is at least start.

key_derivation.description: How this source derived its keys (ADR-0006). 'path' is the weak form -- moving a file looks like a delete plus an add -- and is declared rather than left to be discovered.

root.description: Where the source read from, for a reader. Excluded from run_id: an id embedding an absolute path is an id nobody else can re-derive.

caps.description: Every bound that shortened what this source offered. A cap that shortens coverage appears here rather than being inferred from a shortfall (ADR-0005).

trace_map.description: Where this artefact's TraceMap was written. Outside the folder a consumer ingests, so that a map is not itself ingested as a document.

content_hash.description: The hash of the SOURCE bytes this artefact was converted from -- the same value the trace map's `source.content_hash` carries. Here so that a re-sync can decide whether a unit's bytes changed without opening its sidecar. Optional because a manifest written before it existed omits it; a reader must not infer anything from its absence except that the run was older.

layer.description: What kind of statement this document is, in kiseki's vocabulary. musubi emits 'fact' and 'measure' and never 'interpretation': an interpretation needs a reading, a reading needs a model, and musubi has none (ADR-0010).

removed_sha256.description: The hash of what was taken, and NEVER the value. The removed thing is usually the sensitive thing, and a manifest that quoted it would re-publish, into a file people commit, exactly what the run was for (ADR-0005).

reason.description: A stable token a reader can count and filter on: unknown_format, machinery, too_large, undecodable, no_converter, credential, outside_the_root, directory_symlink.

detail.description: The sentence a person needs. Empty when the reason says it all.

finding.description: What the screener matched, by unit and by kind, and DELIBERATELY NOT WHERE (ADR-0019). A finding points at a credential still in the owner's source file and still valid; an offset and a length in a file people commit is the targeting information an attacker would want, and the owner does not need it to act. The terminal report has both, because a person looking at their own screen is who ADR-0008 stops the run for.

label.description: What to call it in a message: 'an AWS access key id'. 'signature 14 matched' is not actionable.

matched_sha256.description: The hash, and never the value. The run stops so that the secret does not travel; a manifest quoting it would send it to a file instead of a corpus, which is not an improvement.
